Farnaz Fassihi (@farnazfassihi)

BIG SCOOP: US-Israel goal was to install former President Ahmadinejad as Iran's leader (aka Delcy)
An Israeli strike designed to free him from house arrest was part of an effort to bring about regime change and put him in power. w/ @M

Israel’s military actions in Gaza, Lebanon, Iran and beyond “will not bring peace and stability and security for Israel,” argues Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty. Without an independent Palestinian state, “there is no peace and stability in the region.”

Video

In Gaza, “we have to implement all the parts” of the peace plan, says Egypt’s foreign minister, pointing to multiple obstacles, including Israel not allowing enough humanitarian aid in, Hamas refusing to disarm, and Israel not withdrawing. “We are pushing very hard” for Hamas to disarm, he insists.

Video

“The issue of opening the Strait of Hormuz is an integral part of any future agreement” between the US and Iran, says Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty. “The principle of freedom of navigation is extremely important for the world.”

Video

“We are pushing for dialogue” instead of war with Iran, Egypt’s Foreign Minister tells me. “There is no military solution… We’ve been quite clear to condemn all attacks on the Gulf countries, because their security is our security… there is no justification for attacking them.”

Video

“What we are talking about now is hopefully to sign a [memorandum of understanding]” between the US and Iran, Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty tells me. “That could lead the way for setting the parameters, the principles, that would be subject to negotiations later on.”

Video

“We commend President Trump’s wise policies,” Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty tells me, after Trump says he won’t resume strikes on Iran for now. Abdelatty adds he’s hopeful for de-escalation: “Things are moving in the right direction, maybe slowly but steadily.”

Video

Stephen, you will be missed! I’ve loved being on your show. Thank you… Good Night and Good Luck from London.

Happy 1 year of The Ex Files!

From politics & world affairs to personal reflections (and zero fisticuffs!), the exes @amanpour & @JamesP_Rubin have covered just about everything!

Thank you for listening, sharing, and being part of every conversation. Here's to the next chapter!

Video

Huge congratulations to the winners, especially the brave Elaheh and Elnaz Mohammadi, for their truly fearless reporting.


International Women's Media Foundation (@IWMF)

We’re incredibly proud to announce the winners of our 2026 Courage in Journalism Awards: Elaheh and Elnaz Mohammadi of Iran, @ByGeorgiaFort of the United States, and Nay Min Ni of Myanmar.

As Trump embarks on a summit with Xi Jinping seeking help to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. @amanpour  reflects on their last meeting & why Trump is negotiating from a weaker position

Watch Christiane Amanpour Presents: The Ex Files 🗂️ on @globalplayer 🎧

Video

“This mix of indifference and denial is the consequence of decades of occupation, which led to dehumanization of Palestinians.” Israeli historian and scholar of genocide @bartov_omer tells me about the conclusions he reached in his new book, “Israel: What Went Wrong?”.

Video

When she met President Trump, Venezuelan opposition leader @MariaCorinaYA gifted him her Nobel medal. Was it worth it? “Yes,” she tells me. “President Trump is the only head of state that has risked the lives of some of his citizens for freedom and democracy in my country.”

Video

“There have been very important steps taken” by the US in Venezuela, says @MariaCorinaYA. But when will elections be held? “We trust what we’ve heard from the US government,” she tells me, suggesting a possible timetable sooner than the end of Trump’s second term.

Video

Venezuelan Nobel Peace Prize laureate @MariaCorinaYA has been out of her country since she made it to Oslo last December. She has vowed to return, and tells me it will be “as soon as possible,” when security allows.
